resolvedQuestions.text: Q1: Where is the surface order (opencode, obsidian, webflow) encoded, and where are sk-code-obsidian and sk-code-webflow treated as installed?
Q7: F10, which shared/ or sk-code-skilled leaves could serve the stack-agnostic ROUTER.md intents once webflow is deleted, and what is the smallest fix (R6)?
Q2: What breaks when an external user deletes sk-code-obsidian and sk-code-webflow, observed in a throwaway copy, and what happens when they add their own surface?
Q8: F20, what does fixing the compiled-routing re-mint dependency on specs/sk-doc/z_archive/019-skill-routing-refactor/ cost across every hub, versus documenting it (R7 or a reasoned no)?

Q3: How should a user-added surface outrank sk-code-skilled (registry priority field, native or fallback flag, tieBreak derived at mint time, --surface-hint, other), and which option is cheapest at acceptable risk?
Q9: F18, does /create:skill-parent update --surfaces perform the five steps a hand-added surface misses (3d-files, 6b, 5k-alias, 5k-packet, 5k-canary), observed in a throwaway full-tree copy?

ruledOutDirections.text: Hand-editing §11 rows to remove webflow paths — defeats the generated-projection contract (ROUTER.md:41) and the re-mint already does it.

No per-surface `ROUTER.md`/map file found at `find -maxdepth 2` inside the surface packets — the per-packet maps ROUTER.md:41 describes live deeper or are generated; a later iteration (Q9/Q11) can locate the authored source the re-mint reads.

None definitively eliminated. The BREAK-class observation (deleting the two packets in a throwaway copy) was intentionally not attempted: this iteration's focus is the static hub inventory; the deletion experiment is Q2's focus. No throwaway copy was created.

Broad repo-wide order grep before reading the named hub files: the bare-basename glob matched nested packet READMEs first and the 70-hit cap exhausted before the hub-root files; targeted reads were cheaper. (Evidence: grep result counts and file paths in Actions Taken item 4.)

Treating `mode-registry.json:19` `surfaces` array as the ranking: it is a declaration list; the rank lives in `hub-router.json:7` tieBreak plus the `stack-detection.md:39` precedence. Conflating them would misstate the v4.0.0.4 claim's accuracy.
Treating `routeSkillResources` `resources` output as a bug — it faithfully emits the map; the map itself is stale until re-mint.
Re-running the addition half (five new FAILs, 113 → 118): the scaffold + re-mint cycle would exceed the wall clock. Carried, not re-observed (iteration-005.md:24).

Re-asking whether the parent-skill-check failure is deletion-caused: settled directly — exit 0 at baseline with packets present, exit 1 with 113 failures after deletion.
No claim is made about deletion failures. The authorized throwaway-copy experiment is deferred to the Q2 focus.

Expecting the compiled manifest to encode the surface order — it stores policy identity only (row 7).
Treating the minimal hand-copy failures as only five: the probe also exposed failures from duplicate aliases, absent vocabulary classes, and the intentionally stale manifest.

Searching the compiled-routing runtime for a hardcoded surface order: none exists. The order enters as data (hub tieBreak) and leaves as data; only the comparator and the hint reorder are code (rows 1–3, 5).
None new for the strategy list beyond the two ruled-out rows above.

"Move the whole 019 packet into `.skilled/`" — 73MB of spec history/research/real-model logs has no serving role; only the traced closure subset is consumed, and moving a subset splits the archival packet.
"`compiled-route-manifest mint` requires the authored tree" — contradicted by observation: mint targets the runtime root and ran (exit 1 `already-exists`) with `specs/` absent.
`.skilled/README.md` as a documentation surface — the path does not exist (row 10).
Treating the advisor's `webflow cms` disambiguation as surface-order evidence — it routes to mcp-code-mode and penalizes sk-code (row 3).
Reading the advisor as a surface ranker — it has no surface ids and its surfaceHint is a pass-through to `compiled-route.cjs` (rows 4–5).
Treating `compiled-route-guard.cjs` as a re-mintability check: it returned exit 0 with `specs/` absent and checks served-runtime freshness instead.
None newly eliminated beyond the above; the deletion experiment remains Q2's focus and was again not attempted.
None.
Adding only a new directory is sufficient for routing: the custom prompt returned `action=defer` with no targets.
A README-only R1 edit: the scaffold and parent-skill checklist still omit insertion position.
"No re-mint step needed after editing hub-router.json" — contradicted: route output collapsed to `servingAuthority:"legacy"` until `refresh` ran.
None new beyond the ruled-out rows.

`compiled-route-sync.cjs --check` is an executable deletion probe under the required copy recipe: it stops before validation because `specs/` is absent. This limitation was seen previously and is not retried with a different copy shape.
A new doctor order rule as part of minimal R1: 5e/5i have no user/native classification, so enforcing it requires a broader contract.
"R1 = insert surface first in tieBreak" — illegal: 5i enforces workflow-before-surface; correct phrase is "ahead of the default surface" (observed `PASS: 5i` only with that placement shape).
"sync --check catches post-refresh manifest drift" — contradicted: exit 0 while authored and runtime manifests differed (`cmp` exit 1); the guard, not sync, owns that leg.

The mint path cannot be judged inside a `specs`-excluded copy; candidate for the reducer: "re-mint verification requires a full-tree copy" (not promoted to exhausted — one more angle remains).
Treating canary-cases.v1.json as R2 scope: it is generated closure data; re-mint owns it.

Docs-only insertion convention (insert before `sk-code-skilled` in `tieBreak` + `routerSignals`): two lists must agree and have already drifted in a sibling hub; insertion position is unenforced; stale-manifest stub on hand edit (carried).

Hardcoded native-last rule in the shared compiler or runtime: forces the operator's order to change; the Q4 split is data.
"sync --check's printed remediation is sufficient" — the command it names is the one that fails (MOVE-SIMULATION); only the manual authored-path copy-back unblocks it.
A priority/rank field: the existing ordered list expresses the requirement without another schema and ordering source.
"leaf-manifest.json needs hand-editing" — `generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --check` returned `OK` on the scrubbed file, i.e. `--write` produces it.
Deriving order from registry-array position: the registry does not currently define that position as precedence.
--surface-hint as the project default: it is conditional on each caller passing a matched surface hint.

Treating the current `/create:skill-parent update --surfaces` command as a complete removal path; its command contract has no removal option, and the earlier simulations did not clear all doctor legs.
None new beyond the violation forensics: whether the clone carried the writes or the shell cwd reverted could not be settled in budget; the end-state is recorded either way.

Confirmation, not re-entry: `--surface-hint` as the default tie fix stays blocked (strategy §9); the new evidence (matched-only test :79-83, opt-in pass-through) confirms it cannot be the shipped default.
A native/fallback sort flag: one flag cannot order multiple custom surfaces, while the list already can.

None established. Deletion-dependent manual and quality paths still need a bounded throwaway-copy check.
Treating `/doctor:update` as an operator/external split mechanism: its decisions are per-checkout and uniform; no example-unit class and no operator-specific layer exist.

Broad `rg 'webflow|obsidian'` as the dependent set — ~150 hits dominated by `mcp-obsidian` (a different product), the `sk-design` webflow brand bundle, and changelogs; the operative signal is the precise `sk-code-obsidian|sk-code-webflow` pattern.
Treating advisor Obsidian/Webflow marker fixtures as dependencies on installed sk-code packets: the test builds temporary workspaces and asserts the hint value directly.
Treating the archived benchmark PASS as a deletion-test result: its own report has zero eligible/scored rows and routes gold to the Webflow example.
Deriving surface order from the installed packet set inside `/doctor:update`: the engine's unit universe is tree+base paths and it computes file status, not routing order.

A new surface-scaffolding command or separate installer guide: the existing parent-skill workflow already creates surface packets. A new entry point would duplicate its contract.
README-only wording: `SKILL.md:40` is the pointer target every other doc defers to; a README-only edit leaves the hub contract unmarked.

Bare `compiled-route-manifest.cjs refresh` — exits 2 usage; requires `--hub` + `--skill-root`.
